paragraph: An agent that controls rheoTool's solvers on OpenFOAM in words for the start-up of a planar channel flow of an Oldroyd-B fluid: it takes the relaxation time and the polymer viscosity the MD agent handed over, once the person has let the card cross, and the solvent viscosity from the person, holds any value its build did not declare, and, asked for a run, runs the start-up flow on the settings the person gives and reports the centreline velocity against time as the solver writes it, with the analytical solution computed by a library skill beside it.

tool_reading.claim: rheoTool's Oldroyd-B model (TypeName Oldroyd-B, or Oldroyd-BLog for the log-conformation approach) takes the constants etaS, etaP and lambda in constitutiveProperties, with rho, each a dimensioned value in OpenFOAM's SI dimension set (dynamic viscosity, time, density)
rheoFoam is a transient solver whose momentum equation takes fvOptions, and rheoTool supports cyclic patches, so a channel may be driven by a momentum source with periodic ends
loci: the user guide, section 4.7.1, the listing of rheoFoam's momentum equation, and the changelog on cyclicAMI (mat-20261121-rheotool-6.0-user-guide)
tool_reading.limitations: the guide's channel tutorial is steady and inlet-driven; a start-up driven by a source is not exemplified in rheoTool, only in OpenFOAM's own planarPoiseuille tutorial (mat-20261121-openfoam-9-planarpoiseuille-watersking)

tool_reading.claim: the analytical velocity of the start-up planar Poiseuille flow of an Oldroyd-B fluid is Waters and King's series in the elasticity number lambda eta0/(rho h^2) and the solvent's share beta, h the half-width and time scaled by lambda
tool_reading.limitations: the original, Waters and King (1970), was not read: no open copy was found

tool_reading.claim: the image rheotool:of90 is in the Colima profile rheotool, which `colima list` showed stopped on 2026-11-21

rheoFoam's momentum equation is written per unit density: the pressure it solves for and the stress term are divided by the density, so a momentum source given to it in fvModels (semiImplicitSource, volumeMode specific) is a force per unit mass, the pressure gradient over the density
loci: the user guide, section 4.7 on divTau, 'divided by the density to be compliant with the usual strategy of OpenFOAM', and section 5.1.1 on the pressure (mat-20261121-rheotool-6.0-user-guide)
OpenFOAM-9's planarPoiseuille tutorial, constant/fvModels, a semiImplicitSource of volumeMode specific on U (mat-20261121-openfoam-9-planarpoiseuille-watersking, the same tutorial folder)

tool_reading.claim: the run adapter, tried under TMPDIR, sent a periodic planar channel case into rheotool:of90 through stdin, ran blockMesh and rheoFoam there and read back OpenFOAM's probe of the centreline velocity; the series followed oldroyd_b_startup_channel_velocity for the trial's settings, its overshoot and its oscillation included (evidence for the adapter only; no value of it enters a card)
loci: the adapter's trial under TMPDIR, back/log.rheoFoam and back/postProcessing/probes/0/U of its run folder
tool_reading.limitations: one mesh and one time step; the run's own numerical error is not estimated, which a two-resolution run would give (discretization_error_from_two_resolutions)

contract.name: run_startup_channel
contract.description: run rheoFoam (rheoTool on OpenFOAM, in the image rheotool:of90 of the Colima profile rheotool) on the start-up of a planar channel flow of an Oldroyd-B fluid: a channel periodic along the flow between two no-slip walls, the fluid at rest with no stress until the pressure gradient is applied, the constitutive model Oldroyd-BLog with the schemes and solvers of rheoTool's channel tutorial; the case goes into the container through stdin and the results come back through stdout; a new folder under runs/cfd for each run; it returns the centreline velocity against time as the solver writes it and computes nothing from it

half_width.description: h, the distance from the centreline to each wall

solvent_viscosity.description: eta_s, the solvent's viscosity, the person's to give

polymer_viscosity.description: eta_p, the polymer viscosity; the value src/handover.py values prints for the row polymer_viscosity

relaxation_time.description: lambda, the relaxation time; the value src/handover.py values prints for the row relaxation_time

driving.description: -dp/dx, the pressure gradient that drives the flow from rest, applied as a step; rheoFoam takes it over the density

cells_across.description: how many cells span the channel, an odd number so that one cell centre is on the centreline

end_time.description: how long after the start the run ends

probe_every.description: how many time steps between two written values of the probe

budget_s.description: the running time the run may take before the call gives up on it, counted while it runs and not while it is paused; no limit when null

openfoam_version.description: the version OpenFOAM's banner prints in log.rheoFoam

openfoam_build.description: the build OpenFOAM's banner prints in log.rheoFoam

probe_location.description: the probe's point, the channel's centre, in metres

centreline_velocity.description: pairs [t, u]: the time in seconds and the streamwise velocity at the centreline in metres per second, as rheoFoam's probes function writes them

run_dir.description: the run's folder, relative to this directory

inputs.description: the call's inputs, the conditions the run held under

safety_gate.place: src/gate.py, consulted by src/run_tool.py before the call

error_contracts.message: a value the run needs is missing or not one the contract takes
